title: Arpita Singh
summary: Arpita Singh was an Indian artist. Known as a figurative artist and a modernist, she created canvases to have both a story line and a carnival of images arranged in a curiously subversive manner. Her artistic approach can be described as an expedition without destination. Her work reflects her background. She brought her inner vision of emotions to the art inspired by her own background and what she saw around the society that mainly affects women. Her works also include traditional Indian art forms and aesthetics, such as miniature painting and different forms of folk art, which she included them regularly.

title: Cico Harahap
summary: Ezzaq Farrouq "Cico" Harahap Jamaludin was a Malaysian actor. He was famous for his role in Puteri Impian the series (1997-1998), Anak Mami (2002) and Operation Mekong (2016).

title: Peter Jaroš
summary: Peter Jaroš was a Slovak novelist, short-story writer, screenwriter, and film dramaturg. He is best known for the multigenerational novel Tisícročná včela, widely regarded as one of the most important Slovak novels of the second half of the 20th century, and for the screenplays of two of the most popular Slovak films of the communist era, Pacho, hybský zbojník (1975) and The Millennial Bee (1983).

title: Pou Temara

He was professor of Māori language and tikanga Māori (practices) at the University of Waikato, and a cultural authority on whaikōrero (oratory), whakapapa (genealogy) and karakia. Prior to working at Waikato, he taught at Victoria University of Wellington, and at Te Whare Wānanga o Awanuiārangi. He was latterly professor of Māori philosophy at Awanuiārangi. He was a member of the Ngāi Tūhoe iwi (tribe).

He declared his affiliation with the Russian Orthodox Church Outside of Russia (ROCOR) and the Russian Old-Orthodox Church (ROCC).
